newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Casualty figures vary in Sri Lanka attack.
newsitem.headline: Casualty figures vary in Sri Lanka attack.

text.p: Sporadic fighting continued in the northern Sri Lankan town of Paranthan on Friday, a day after government forces repelled a major attack by separatist Tamil rebels, military officials said.

Sri Lankan security forces were consolidating their position after the rebels overran parts of the town's defences in fierce fighting on Thursday, which left more than 500 guerrillas dead or wounded, the Defence Ministry said.
"Forces are mopping up the last of the resistance," an army official in Colombo said.
The rebels were not immediately available for comment, but a London-based spokesmen for the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) on Thursday denied the 500 figure.
The bodies of 60 government soldiers had been recovered by Thursday night, the Ministry of Defence said. The battle left 232 other soldiers wounded, some seriously, it added.
"We're still in the process of evacuating casualties, so there still could be dead and wounded in the area of the attack," military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga said.
Officials said the death toll could rise as scores of badly wounded soldiers were flown from the battlefront to hospitals in the capital Colombo.

Rebel transmissions monitored by the army indicated the rebels had recovered 76 bodies of their fighters. Rebels claimed to have killed more than 100 soldiers, according to military officials in the region.

Intercepted LTTE radio transmissions also said some artillery guns, armoured cars and tanks had been destroyed by the rebels, who used human-wave tactics and suicide bombers to overrun defences at Paranthan, a junction town 280 km (185 miles) north of Colombo.
Jayatunga said soldiers had destroyed several artillery pieces to prevent them from falling into rebel hands. He did not say how many.
Paranthan is the first military base to be attacked this year by the LTTE, who are fighting for a homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
Paranthan sits astride the main north-south highway from Colombo to Jaffna and controls the road junction connecting the rebel-held northeastern town of Mullaitivu.

Security forces officials told Reuters the rebels may have planned to cut off government-controlled Paranthan and Kilinochchi, just south of Paranthan, from the army's main bases in the northern Jaffna peninsula.
"They probably wanted to cut off these two towns from the north, isolate them and hammer them. But they were not successful," one official said.

Government forces, which captured Paranthan from the rebels last July, pushed further into LTTE territory and took control of Kilinochchi in August, the last major town controlled by the rebels. The rebels have vowed to take back both towns.
In July last year, the rebels overran a key army base at Mullaitivu, killing or capturing more than 1,000 men, dealing the military its biggest blow in the war, now in its 14th year.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the conflict. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
